claim: NASA published satellite-based tracking of Antarctic iceberg A-81 near South Georgia, illustrating time-dependent geospatial interpretation.
verifiedFacts: NASA Earth Observatory published an October 27 image-of-the-day report about iceberg A-81 near South Georgia.
The featured MODIS Terra image was acquired October 20, 2026, distinct from its publication date.
The article reports that the iceberg slowed near South Georgia's underwater shelf; the account cites scientific observers and prior imagery.
inference: This is a strong low-cost demonstrator for distinguishing observation time, publication time, interpretation and uncertainty.
Potential client problem: environmental dashboards blur satellite acquisition dates with present conditions; consultancy concept: temporal-provenance geospatial storyboard.
significance: The difference between satellite capture time and reporting time is a concrete lesson in temporal evidence and environmental visualization.
actorRefs: NASA Earth Observatory:research publisher; NASA Terra:observation provider; scientists:analysts
assumptions: NASA image reuse and attribution can be reviewed for an educational prototype.
knownLimitations: Single image does not prove continuous motion or current iceberg location.
Ecological impacts near South Georgia are not established by this report.
